titles.385: Annotatio II NATIVITAS open: Inventors among Berengar’s confuters — PRIORIS Rupert of Deutz
titles.386: Annotatio II NATIVITAS: Rupert’s Genesis gold/fire analogy — bread still bread, yet truly Christ
titles.387: Annotatio II NATIVITAS: Rupert’s Exodus — bread/wine substance joined, not destroyed, into body-unity
titles.388: Annotatio II NATIVITAS: Cuno of Siegburg — accomplice and patron of Rupert’s sentence

latin.385: Ceterum inter Berengarii Confutatores tam Crassioris, quam Subtilioris Consubstantiationis Inventores, nullo negotio repereris. PRIORIS quidem RUPERTUM TUITIENSEM Abbatem, fassô Johanne Gerhardô, Patrolog. p. 551. nequicquam ergò vel Reformatis, à Reverendiss. Forbesio, vel Lutheranis, nisi in contumeliam, a Bajero Disput. de Impanat. num. 11. 21. & 22. annumeratum, cum ipse Rupertus semet crassum Impanatorem expositione sententiae suae prodat.
latin.386: Tum Commentario in Genesin Lib. 6. cap. 32. his verbis tradito: Quomodo, inquit, panis, qui videtur, est Christus? ad hæc inquam, quomodo qualibet metalli species v. g. aurum sive argentum (nota tamen hîc similitudinem Fratribus Augustanae confessionis usitatam, praecipuè de ferro) valido igni conflatum atque resolutum, re vera & aurum est, & ignis quoque dicitur & est? Etenim aurum videtur & est, quod erat, & tamen verissimè ignis dicitur & est, quod non erat: Idcirco sic omnino panis admotus vel immersus terribili atque ineffabili mysterio passionis Christi, adhuc panis videtur esse, quod erat, & tamen in veritate Christus est, quod non erat.
latin.387: Tum Commentario in Exodum, Lib. 2. cap. 10. expositione auctiori: Sicut, inquit, humanam naturam non destruxit, cùm illam operatione sua ex utero virginis DEUS verbo in unitatem personae conjunxit; Sic SUBSTANTIAM panis & vini, secundum exteriorem speciem, quinque sensibus subactam, non mutat aut destruit, cum eidem Verbo, in UNITATEM corporis ejusdem, quod in cruce pependit, & sanguinis ejusdem quem de latere suo fudit, ista CONJUNGIT. Ibidem: Proinde sicut hominem, ait, qui de virgine sumtus in cruce pependit, rectè & Catholicè Deum confitemur, sic veraciter hoc, quod sumimus de sancto altari, Christum dicimus, agnum Dei praedicamus.
latin.388: CUNONEM etiam Abbatem Sigebergensem, complicem & fautorem sententiae suae nactum, utpote de quo, in praefatione, libris suis, de operibus Trinitatis in Genesin & Exodum, praefixa, inter alia scribit, quòd solus CUNO, imò per Cunonem, (ut ait) Christus praesidio sibi adfuit contra eos, qui molesti fuere huic operi, & qui tùm dictis tùm factis, fremuerunt in ipsum, quasi paxillus sibi Cuno factus sit, positus in loco fideli, in quo spei suae possit vasculum suspendi.
latin.389: Sed & reperias vice versâ, eodem seculo undecimo, qui sententiam hanc hæresin appellarunt & in ipsa herba suffocare annisi sunt, GUITMUNDUM scil. Aversanum, de exortu modò dictae sententiae, ita scribentem, libro 3. de veritate corporis & sanguinis Domini contra Berengarium: Nunc, inquit, contra illos habenda est ratio qui Ecclesiae rationibus expugnati, jam quidem negare nequeunt substantiam corporis Christi cibo inesse Dominico; panem tamen & vinum per verba Salvatoris in carnem ejus & sanguinem verti nequaquam credentes, sed Christum PANI ET VINO COMMISCENTES, tanquam subtiliori ratione, HÆRESIN ALTERAM condiderunt. … Quapropter … nec alias ipsi afferant, quae insania est, ut Christum, ut ita dixerim, sua autoritate IMPANENT ET INVINENT. … At IMPANARI & INVINARI Christum, nulla … expetit ratio, nec Prophetae praedixerunt, nec Christus ostendit, nec Apostoli praedicaverunt, nec mundus, exceptis his paucissimis HÆRETICIS, credidit. … Christus enim isti IMPANATUM ET INVINATUM annunciant … Hos IMPANATORES suos ipse Dominus Jesus ore suo interficit cum accipiens panem … ait, Hoc est Corpus meum; non ait: IN HOC LATET corpus meum; nec dixit: IN HOC vino est sanguis meus.
latin.390: Guitmundo meritò adjungimus ALGERUM ex Scholastico & Ecclesiastico monachum, eandem Impanationis sententiam, novae hæreseos, hisce postulantem: Quamvis, inquit, Sacramentum à re Sacramenti tanquam figura à veritate satis distinctum sit, errantes tamen quidam, de quibusdam sanctorum verbis dicunt ita personaliter IMPANATUM Christum, sicut in carne humana, personaliter incarnatum Deum, quae HÆRESIS, quia nova & absurda est, rationibus & autoritatibus radicitus est exstirpanda.

pass_a.385: For the rest, among Berengar’s Confuters you will find without trouble Inventors both of the Crasser and of the Subtler Consubstantiation. Of the FORMER indeed Rupert Abbot of Deutz, John Gerhard confessing (Patrology p. 551) — therefore numbered neither by the Reformed, by the Most Reverend Forbes, nor by the Lutherans except in contumely, by Bayer’s Disputation on Impanation nos. 11, 21, and 22 — since Rupert himself betrays himself a crass Impanator by the exposition of his own sentence.
pass_a.386: Then in the Commentary on Genesis bk. 6 ch. 32 handed down in these words: How, he says, is the bread which is seen Christ? To this I say, how is any species of metal, e.g. gold or silver (note here nonetheless the similitude usual with the Brothers of the Augsburg Confession, especially of iron) fused and resolved by a strong fire, in truth both gold and also called and is fire? For the gold is seen and is what it was, and yet most truly is called and is fire, which it was not: Therefore so altogether the bread brought near or immersed in the terrible and ineffable mystery of Christ’s passion still seems to be bread, which it was, and yet in truth is Christ, which it was not.
pass_a.387: Then in the Commentary on Exodus bk. 2 ch. 10 with a fuller exposition: Just as, he says, He did not destroy human nature when by His operation from the virgin’s womb GOD by the Word joined it into unity of person; So He does not change or destroy the SUBSTANCE of bread and wine, according to the exterior species subject to the five senses, when He JOINS these to the same Word into the UNITY of the same body which hung on the cross, and of the same blood which He poured from His side. In the same place: Therefore just as we rightly and Catholicly confess as God the man who, taken from the virgin, hung on the cross, so truly we call Christ this which we take from the holy altar, we preach the Lamb of God.
pass_a.388: He also got CUNO Abbot of Siegburg as accomplice and favorer of his sentence — of whom, in the preface prefixed to his books On the works of the Trinity on Genesis and Exodus, he writes among other things that CUNO alone, nay through Cuno (as he says) Christ was present to him as a guard against those who were troublesome to this work and who both by words and deeds roared against him — as if Cuno had been made a peg for him, set in a faithful place, on which he might hang the vessel of his hope.
pass_a.389: But you will also find on the contrary side, in the same eleventh century, those who called this sentence a heresy and tried to smother it in the very blade — namely Guitmund of Aversa, writing thus on the rise of the sentence just named, in book 3 On the truth of the Lord’s body and blood against Berengar: Now, he says, account must be had against those who, stormed by the Church’s reasons, can no longer deny that the substance of Christ’s body is in the Lord’s food; yet by no means believing that bread and wine are turned by the Savior’s words into His flesh and blood, but MIXING Christ WITH BREAD AND WINE, as by a subtler reason, they founded ANOTHER HERESY. … Wherefore … let them not bring other [causes], which is madness, that they should by their own authority, so to speak, IMPANATE AND INVINATE Christ. … But that Christ be IMPANATED and INVINATED no reason demands … nor did the Prophets foretell, nor Christ show, nor the Apostles preach, nor the world believe, except these very few HERETICS. … For they announce an IMPANATED AND INVINATED Christ … These His IMPANATORS the Lord Jesus Himself kills with His mouth when taking bread … He says, This is My Body; He does not say: IN THIS LIES My body; nor did He say: IN THIS wine is My blood.
pass_a.390: To Guitmund we rightly join ALGER, from Scholastic and Ecclesiastical a monk, demanding the same Impanation sentence as a new heresy in these words: Although, he says, the Sacrament is sufficiently distinct from the Thing of the Sacrament as figure from truth, yet certain erring ones say from certain words of the saints that Christ is so personally IMPANATED as God is personally incarnate in human flesh — which HERESY, because it is new and absurd, is to be rooted out by reasons and authorities.

385: Among Berengar’s confuters you easily find inventors of both crasser and subtler Consubstantiation.
Of the crasser: Rupert, Abbot of Deutz — Gerhard owns him; Forbes and Bayer list him only as insult — because Rupert’s own exposition brands him a crass Impanator.
386: Genesis commentary (VI.32): how is visible bread Christ? Like gold in strong fire — still gold to sight, yet truly called and is fire.
So bread brought into Christ’s passion-mystery still seems bread, yet in truth is Christ — a similitude Augsburg brothers later use of iron.
387: Exodus commentary (II.10): as God did not destroy human nature when joining it into personal unity from the virgin’s womb, so He does not destroy bread-and-wine substance when joining it to the Word into unity of the crucified body and shed blood.
What we take from the altar we truly call Christ, the Lamb of God — as we confess the virgin-born man on the cross to be God.
388: Rupert names Cuno, Abbot of Siegburg, accomplice and patron of his sentence.
In the Genesis/Exodus preface Christ stood by him through Cuno alone against those who roared at the work — Cuno a peg in a faithful place for the vessel of his hope.
389: Same eleventh century, the other way: Guitmund of Aversa calls the sentence a heresy to smother in the blade.
Beaten from denying Christ’s body in the Lord’s food, some mix Christ with bread and wine and found another heresy — Impanate and Invinate by their own authority.
No prophet, Christ, apostle, or world taught Impanation; the Lord kills Impanators with This is My Body — not In this lies My body.
390: Alger joins Guitmund: some erring readers make Christ personally Impanated as God is personally Incarnate — a new absurd heresy to root out by reason and authority.
